Hints: Use the top of the unit circle.|The point is (0, 1).
Solution: At angle theta, the unit-circle point is (cos(theta),sin(theta)). Read the requested coordinate at the cardinal angle. sin(pi/2) = 1.

Hints: Use the 30-degree special angle.|Cosine is the larger coordinate there.
Solution: Find the acute reference angle, use its special-angle cosine, then choose the sign of the unit-circle x-coordinate in the given quadrant. cos(pi/6) = sqrt(3)/2.
Use tan(theta)=sin(theta)/cos(theta) where cosine is nonzero. For special angles, divide the exact sine and cosine values. tan(pi/4) = 1.

Hints: Sine is an odd function.|The sign changes.
Solution: On the unit circle, reversing the angle negates the y-coordinate and preserves the x-coordinate. Thus sine is odd and cosine is even. Adding pi negates both coordinates and preserves their ratio, so tangent has period pi wherever defined. sin(-theta) = -sin(theta).
